General Mills Considering Separation of Haagen-Dazs Business Outside North America
By Aimee Look and Ben Dummett

General Mills is considering separating from its Haagen-Dazs ice-cream business outside of North America, in a move that could potentially lead to a sale, according to people familiar with the matter.
Planning is at an early stage and General Mills, best known for such brands as Cheerios and Lucky Charms, could ultimately retain the business, the people said.
General Mills owns and runs the Haagen-Dazs business outside of North America, including in Europe and other markets such as Thailand, Mexico and the United Arab Emirates.

Froneri, owned by private-equity firm PAI Partners, Nestle and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, operates Haagen-Dazs in the U.S. That could make it a logical buyer for the General Mills business, one of the people said.

The review of the General Mills' business follows its decision in June to sell shops it owns under the Haagen-Dazs brand in mainland China to an investor group. General Mills said it will retain Haagen-Dazs's retail operations in the country.

The packaged-foods giant is in the midst of an executive handover, with Chief Executive Officer Jeff Harmening expected to hand the reins to Dana McNabb in January. McNabb, who is currently chief operating officer, has said she will be focused on company-wide sales revival and cost cutting.

Other food conglomerates have shed ice-cream operations as a cost cutting measure, citing supply-chain mismatch and operational drag. Unilever spun off its business into Magnum Ice Cream, while Nestle said in February would offload the rest of its ice-cream unit.
General Mills generated sales of around $18.4 billion for fiscal 2026, down 5% on year. Its super-premium ice-cream category had $782.7 million in sales for the year.
The potential sale price for the operations couldn't be learned.
